scope: Complete frozen compiler-backed jsoup census after enum-reference corrections. Known development repository and already inspected misses; not held-out, independent human review, whole-graph precision or god-object classification.

oracle.nonSourceCategories: Retain external fields, array lengths and class literals separately, as in the unchanged oracle.

candidate: Build and freeze a release candidate after native regression/gates. Record exact production sources, commit, manifests, build settings and binary hash before extraction. No package version bump.

comparison.sourcePolicy: Read-only pinned clean repository; entire original extraction scope, fresh outputs for each frozen release binary. The source oracle only scores its registered 88-file Java 8 cohort; retain other graph records separately. Preserve all failures and graph omission warnings. Timing is operational only; no performance conclusion from these two observations.

scoring: Use the unchanged compiler capture, UTF-16 to UTF-8 conversion, exact target declaration and source owner joins. Retain the complete 3785 ordinary plus 529 enum-reference denominator.

Inventory every returned field/enum contact in the registered source files, including extra, wrong, ambiguous, unanchored and unmapped contacts. Any unsupported new contact requires source review and a correction before claiming precision.

Run the fresh pre-enum baseline against the same frozen oracle; compare its whole graph to the original preserved Compass graph and disclose differences instead of assuming equality. Preserve all original results.

Report declaration joins, exact target-plus-owner occurrence recall, every miss and all precision failures separately for ordinary fields and enum constants; Graphify keeps its frozen environment and graph.
Compare whole graph additions/removals, identities, edge direction/multiplicity/provenance and omission warnings; do not infer functional community quality from graph changes.
Repeat complete verification and compare report bytes. Repeated verifier agreement is consistency evidence, not an independent source oracle.
limitations: This is one known Java configuration; general cross-language superiority remains unproven.
The change was motivated by observed missed enum constants. All scores are development results, even though this follow-up protocol precedes candidate extraction.
